title: Consumer confidence rebounds on income hopes while living standards remain flat and housing, inflation, and rates keep shaping perceived room
source_unit: Bank of Korea, Consumer Survey Index for September 2026; official release indexed by Korea Development Institute Economic Information and Education Center
geography: South Korea; urban household consumer survey

observations.period: September 2026; consumer sentiment and component movement

denominator.unit: responding Korean urban households from 2,500 sampled households

sentiment_room_split.value: Macro and income expectations improved more than current living-standards assessment, separating confidence about direction from present household room

observations.method: Bank of Korea monthly Consumer Survey Index, with the CCSI constructed from six standardized consumer-attitude components; survey conducted September 9-16, 2026.
observations.uncertainty: The index is a subjective expectation measure and is not a transaction, retail-sales, income, or household-panel measure. Monthly movement can reflect market news, policy expectations, seasonality, and geopolitical events.
observations.subgroup: Urban Korean households; component estimates and detailed subgroup tables are in the linked release attachment.
observations.counterinterpretation: A rebound above the long-run benchmark may indicate improved expectations without current material improvement; unchanged living-standards assessment is a counterweight to the composite headline.

past_year_inflation_perception.unit: percent perceived consumer-price increase over the past year

inflation_expectations_change.value: All listed expected-inflation horizons were unchanged from August

price_meaning.value: Stable inflation expectations can coexist with a high perceived price level and continued household sensitivity to cost

observations.method: Monthly household survey measures of perceived past inflation and expected inflation over one-, three-, and five-year horizons.
observations.uncertainty: Perceived and expected inflation are not estimates of individual household inflation or future realized CPI; question framing, salient prices, and recent purchase experience can affect responses.
observations.subgroup: Korean urban households; release-level aggregate estimates.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stable expectations may reflect anchored beliefs, limited information, or adaptation to higher prices rather than restored purchasing power.

housing_price_outlook_index.unit: housing-price outlook CSI reported for September

interest_rate_outlook_index.unit: interest-rate outlook CSI reported for September

housing_cost_meaning.value: Improved general sentiment can coexist with persistent housing-price expectations and stronger concern about interest-rate conditions

observations.method: Consumer Survey Index subcomponents for housing-price, interest-rate, and wage-level expectations.
observations.uncertainty: These are expectations, not transaction prices, mortgage approvals, debt-service burdens, or realized housing mobility. Aggregate housing expectations can diverge sharply by tenure, region, age, and wealth.
observations.subgroup: Korean urban households; release-level aggregate estimates.
observations.counterinterpretation: High housing-price expectations may express fear of being priced out or a desire to preserve asset value, not optimism about household affordability.

observations.period: September 2026; survey design and interpretation boundary

composite_components.value: Current living standards, prospective living standards, prospective household income, prospective household spending, current domestic economic conditions, and prospective domestic economic conditions

consumer_sentiment_boundary.value: The release is a leading-expectations layer that must be paired with realized spending, prices, credit, employment, and housing transactions

observations.method: Monthly cross-sectional urban household survey conducted by the Bank of Korea; sample and response counts reported in the release materials.
observations.uncertainty: Nonresponse, sampling, index construction, and short field window limit interpretation. The release does not follow the same household through later purchases or financial outcomes.
observations.counterinterpretation: A high response rate does not eliminate coverage or measurement limits, and a composite index can conceal offsetting component movements.

related_sources.claim: Bank of Korea statistical calendar identifies the September 2026 Consumer Survey Index release.
KOSIS dashboard describes the Consumer Survey Index as a measure of perceptions and future consumption outlook.

boundary: This record adds a non-U.S. consumer-expectations route: composite sentiment, household living-standard perceptions, inflation expectations, housing-price expectations, and interest-rate concern can move on different margins. It does not establish realized consumption, affordability, household debt stress, housing transactions, or causal effects of policy or markets.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: KDI official policy-material page indexing the Bank of Korea September 2026 Consumer Survey release, plus the Bank of Korea statistical calendar and corroborating published summary for sample, index, expectation, and field-period details.
reproduction_audit.version_note: The linked KDI page is an official Korean-language index page; the underlying ten-page Bank of Korea attachment is identified as D26090163.pdf. Detailed component values should be rechecked against that attachment if the download endpoint becomes available.
